Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:10:1.hebrew: דלמא רחומי רחים - הואיל ולכולן הוי ולדות, אלא ודאי, אפי' ילדה אינה מרחמת אלא שלה. ומשני: במקום דידה כו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:10:1.english: Perhaps it is merciful - Since all of them have offspring, [why shouldn't we be concerned?] Rather, certainly, even [if] it gave birth, it is merciful only to its own. And [the Gemara] answers: In a place [where it has] its own, etc.:

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:11:1.hebrew: הדבר בחזקתו וכן - כלומר, דקתני סיפא: וכך היה רשב"ג אומר: הנכנס כו' — מאי לאו, מדסיפא, דקתני וכן כו':
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:11:1.english: The matter stands in its presumptive status, and similarly - That is to say, since the latter clause teaches: “And thus Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel would say: One who enters...”, etc., is it not [evident] from the latter clause, which teaches “and similarly”, etc.?

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:11:2.hebrew: ודאי דידה - דכל חדא וחדא התלוי בה דידה הויא, דהא אמרת: במקום דידה לא שבקא דידה ומרחמא דלאו דידה. רישא נמי, דקתני הדבר בחזקתו, בודאי דידה מחזקינן לה, ולענין אותו ואת בנו נמי לקי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:11:2.english: Certainly its own - For each and every [mother animal], [the young] clinging to it is its own, for you said: In the presence of its own [offspring], it does not abandon its own and show mercy to [one] that is not its own. In the first clause as well, which teaches [that] the matter stands in its presumptive status, we presume it to certainly be its own, and regarding [the prohibition of] “it and its offspring,” [one who slaughters both on the same day] would also receive lashes.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:12:1.hebrew: הא כדאיתא - וסיפא ודאי, רישא ספק:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:12:1.english: This is as it is - And the latter clause [deals with a case of] certainty, [while] the first clause [deals with a case of] uncertainty.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:12:2.english: And what is [the meaning of] "And similarly"? - Since they are not similar [to each other].

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:12:3.hebrew: ומשני לפטורא - להא דמו: דכי היכי דסיפא פטורות ודאי — דהא ודאי נקבות תלויות במבכירות, דלא שבקא דידה דקאי קמה ומרחמא דלאו דידה — רישא נמי פטורות מן הבכורות ודאי, דא"נ לא דידה הוא, יהא יולדת אחרינא, ואינה מרחמת אלא אם כן יולדת. ולעולם לענין אותו ואת בנו — ספק:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:12:3.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Regarding exemption - In this [respect] they are similar: Just as in the latter clause [the mothers] are definitely exempt — for it is certain that the females are nursing from the first-time mothers, since [a mother] would not leave her own [offspring] that stands before her and show affection to [one] that is not hers — in the first clause as well, they are definitely exempt from [the law of] the firstborn; for even if [the offspring] is not hers, she must have given birth to another, and she does not show affection [to nurse] unless she has given birth. And in truth, regarding the matter of “it and its offspring,” [it remains] in doubt.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:13:1.hebrew: שכרוך אחר רחל - שדבוק אחריה, ומניקתו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:13:1.english: That was trailing after a ewe - That it clings to her, and she nurses it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:13:2.english: Exempt from [the law of] the firstborn - And the [offspring] that comes after it is not a firstborn.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:13:3.hebrew: עד יבא ויורה צדק לכם - עד שיבא אליהו ויורה אם מותר, אם אסור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:13:3.english: Until he comes and instructs righteousness to you - Until Elijah comes and instructs whether it is permitted or forbidden.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:14:1.hebrew: כר' שמעון - לא מרחמא דלא דידה, והאי חזיר גופיה לא קדוש, דנדמה הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:14:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Shimon - [An animal] does not care for [an offspring] that is not hers, and this pig itself is not sanctified, as it is a creature that resembles [another species].

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:14:2.hebrew: ואסור באכילה כרבנן - דחיישינן לרחומי, דאי כרשב"ג, הוה טמא היוצא מן הטהור ומותר באכילה, כדאמרן בפירקין קמא (דף ה:):
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:14:2.english: And forbidden for consumption, in accordance with the Rabbis - For we are concerned about [the animal showing] affection [to another's young]; for if [it were] in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, it would be an unclean [animal] that emerged from a clean [animal] and permitted for consumption, as we said in our first chapter (daf 5b):

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:15:1.hebrew: מאי יבא ויורה - כיון דכרבנן ס"ל, דחיישי לרחומי — מאי "יבא ויורה"? גלוי מילתא הוא — שיגיד לנו אם בנה הוא אם לאו, והוראה לא שייך למימר אלא בדבר הלכה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:15:1.english: What [is the reason for]: “He comes and instructs” - Since he holds in accordance with the Rabbis, who are concerned for [nursing out of] affection, why [does it say]: “He comes and instructs”? It is [merely] a clarification of the facts — that he should tell us whether it is her offspring or not — and [the term] “instruction” is applicable to say only regarding a matter of halakha.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:15:2.hebrew: עד שיודע הדבר - אם בנה הוא, אם לא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:15:2.english: Until the matter becomes known - Whether it is its offspring, or whether [it is] not.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:16:1.hebrew: וכי תימא מספקא ליה כו' - וה"ק: עד שיבא ויורה, אי הלכה כר"ש ומותר באכילה, אי כרבנן ואסור באכילה מספיקא שמא ריחמתו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:16:1.english: And if you would say that it is uncertain to him, etc. - And this is what it means: [He said,] “Until he comes and instructs” [to resolve] whether the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, and [it is] permitted for consumption, or in accordance with the Rabbis, and [it is] forbidden for consumption out of doubt, lest [the ewe merely] had mercy on it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:17:1.hebrew: לעולם פשיטא ליה הלכה כר' שמעון - דפטורה מן הבכורה, דודאי א"נ לאו דידה הוא, אי לאו דהוה לה ולד לא הויא מרחמא ליה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:17:1.english: Actually, it is obvious to him that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon [ben Gamliel] - That [the ewe] is exempt from [the law of] the firstborn, for certainly, even if [the offspring] is not hers, if she had not had an offspring, she would not have shown mercy to it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:17:2.hebrew: ומיהו מספקא ליה אי סבר ר"ש כו' - והיינו "עד יבא ויורה צדק" — ויעמידנו על טעמו של רשב"ג:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:17:2.english: But it is uncertain if Rabbi Shimon holds, etc. - And this is [the meaning of] “until he comes and instructs righteousness” — and he will enlighten us as to the reasoning of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:17:3.hebrew: יולדת מרחמת - והאי אסור באכילה, דלענין בכורה מיפטר, משום דאי הוה דידה — שפיר, ואם לאו דידה — הוה לה אחרינא; ובאכילה אסור, דאיכא למימר: ולד אחרינא הוה לה ומית, ורחמתיה להאי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:17:3.english: An animal that has given birth is merciful - And [therefore] this [creature] is forbidden for consumption. For regarding the firstborn, [the mother] is exempt, because if it was hers, [it is] fine, and if [it was] not hers, she had another [offspring]; but regarding consumption, [it is] forbidden, because it can be said: She had another offspring and it died, and she showed mercy to this one.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:17:4.hebrew: או אינה מרחמת - ומותר באכילה, דודאי דידה הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:17:4.english: Or is not merciful - And [therefore] it is permitted to be eaten, for it is certainly hers.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:18:1.hebrew: (דאי) לאשמעינן טלה וללקו עליה משום אותו ואת בנו - ולימא: ראה טלה כרוך ברחל — פטורה מן הבכורה ממה נפשך: אי האי לאו דידה — אחרינא הוה ליה ומית, ורחמיתא האי; משום אותו בנו לא לקי, עד יבא ויורה לנו טעמו של רבן שמעון:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:18:1.english: (For had he) taught [the case of] a lamb, and let [one] be flogged for it on account of “it and its offspring” - And let him say: “[If] one saw a lamb trailing after a ewe, [she] is exempt from [the law of] the firstborn, whichever way you look at it: if this [lamb] is not hers, she had another [offspring] that died, and she showed mercy to this one; [and] on account of [the prohibition of] ‘it and its offspring,’ [one] is not flogged, until [Elijah] comes and instructs us as to the reasoning of Rabban Shimon.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:18:2.hebrew: הוה אמינא אפי' אם תימצי לומר - יולדת מרחמת — הני מילי דמינה; אבל חזיר מותר באכילה, דלאו דמינה לא מרחמא, והא ודאי בנה הואי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:18:2.english: I would say: Even if you say - [That] an animal that has given birth is merciful — this applies [only] to its own species; but [the] pig [would be] permitted to be eaten, as [a mother animal] does not show mercy to [an animal] not of its species, and this [creature] was certainly its offspring.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:1:1.hebrew: הלכה כר' יוסי בן המשולם למה לי - הא מהך שמעת מינה דהלכתא כוותיה, דהא לא פליגי רבנן עליה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:1:1.english: Why do I [need him to state that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam? - Behold, from that [statement] you deduce that the halakha is in accordance with him, for the Rabbis do not disagree with him.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:2:1.hebrew: אי אמר הלכה בכוליה פירקין ולא אמר - לקמן: "הלכה כר' יוסי", הוה אמינא: "הלכה בכוליה פירקין" — אדרבי יוסי קאי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:2:1.english: Had [Rav] said the halakha throughout the whole chapter, and had not said - below: "The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei," I would have said: "The halakha throughout the whole chapter" refers to Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:2:2.hebrew: ומאי בכוליה פירקין - דמשמע טובא: משום דר' יוסי תרתי מילי אמר במתני' — עושה מקום לקופיץ, וכן תולש את השער לראות את מקום המום. אבל אדרבן שמעון לא אמר רב, דהוא אמר "בר מפלוגתא", ואדרבן שמעון איכא פלוגתא בברייתא, ופלוגתא היא. להכי אשמועינן "הלכה כר' יוסי" בהדיא, לגלויי ולמימרא דאדרבן שמעון בן גמליאל קאי האי "הלכתא בכוליה פירקין", ופלוגתא דבריית' לאו פלוגתא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:2:2.english: And what is "throughout the whole chapter" - Which implies multiple [rulings]: Because Rabbi Yosei stated two matters in the Mishnah: "Clearing a space for the cleaver," and "likewise, one plucks the hair to inspect the site of the blemish." But Rav would not have spoken concerning Rabban Shimon [ben Gamliel], as he [Rav] said, "Except where there is a dispute," and concerning Rabban Shimon there is a dispute in a Baraita, and [one would think that] it is [considered] a dispute. For this reason, he explicitly taught us that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, to reveal and state that this [ruling of] "the halakha is throughout the whole chapter" refers to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, and a dispute in a Baraita is not [considered] a dispute.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:4:1.english: [It] is merciful - It loves the offspring of its fellow [animal].

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:5:1.hebrew: ומצא זכרים - שנולדים עכשיו, תלויין וכרוכין ויונקין הזקנות שנפטרו כבר מן הבכורה, ונקבות הנולדות עכשיו מצא תלויות במבכירות — דהשתא אין כאן לכהן כלום, דבזכרים אין שום בכור, שהרי בני הזקנות הן, ונקבות התלויות במבכירות — אין דין בכורות נוהגת בהן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:5:1.english: And found males - That were newly born, attached, clinging to, and nursing from the older animals that were already exempt from the law of the firstborn; and newly born females he found attached to the first-time mothers, so that now there is nothing here for the priest, for among the males there is no firstborn at all, since they are the offspring of the older animals, and as for the females attached to the first-time mothers, the law of the firstborn does not apply to them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:5:2.hebrew: אין חוששין - להחמיר ולספקן בספק בכורות, ולומר: שמא בנה של זו בא לו אצל זו, וזכרים בני המבכירות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:5:2.english: We are not concerned - To be stringent and treat them as doubtful firstborns, saying: Perhaps the offspring of this [mother] came to that [mother], and the males are the offspring of the first-time mothers.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:6:1.english: That it does not show mercy - [To] the offspring of another animal.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:6:2.hebrew: אא"כ יולדת - אם היה לה וולד מתחלה להאי, ודאי א"נ לא הוי האי וולד דידה — פטורה מן הבכורה, דהא הוה לה אחרינא. ומיהו, היכא דילדה, חיישינן לרחומי — שמרחמת וולד בהמה אחריתי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:6:2.english: Unless it has given birth - If it had an offspring prior to this [subsequent] one, certainly, even if this [nursing] offspring is not its own, [the animal] is exempt from [the law of] the firstborn, for behold, it had another [offspring]. However, where it gave birth, we are concerned about [its tendency to] show mercy — that it shows mercy to the offspring of another animal.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:7:1.hebrew: למאי נפקא מינה - הא לענין בכורה, ממה נפשך פטורה; דאי האי לאו דידה — הא הוה לה אחרינא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:7:1.english: What difference is there - Behold, regarding the matter of the firstborn, whichever way you look at it [the animal] is exempt; for if this [offspring] is not hers, surely she had another [offspring previously].

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:7:2.hebrew: למילקי עליה - דהאי שכרוך אחריה, משום אותו ואת בנו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:7:2.english: To be flogged for it - For [slaughtering] this [offspring] that is trailing after it, on account of [the prohibition of] "it and its offspring".

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:7:3.english: [He] is not flogged - For perhaps it is not hers.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:8:1.hebrew: אין חוששין כו' - אלמא, בודאי דילה מחזיק ליה, דלא מרחמא אלא דידה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:8:1.english: One does not need to be concerned, etc. - Evidently, he certainly presumes it [to be] hers, for it shows affection only to its own.

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:8:2.english: Does it teach - [That] one does not suspect that perhaps it is the offspring of another?

Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:8:3.hebrew: היה קתני - והכי קאמר: ממה נפשך פטורה מן הבכורה, דאין חוששין שמא מרחמא בן חברתה אלא א"כ היה לה וולד אחר מעיקרא. הלכך, לענין בכורה ודאי פטורה, אבל לענין אותו ואת בנו ספיקא הואי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 24a:8:3.english: It teaches "it was" - And this is what it is saying: Whichever way you look at it, [the animal] is exempt from [the law of] the firstborn, for we do not suspect that perhaps it shows affection to the offspring of another unless it [already] had another offspring initially. Therefore, regarding [the law of] the firstborn, it is certainly exempt, but regarding [the prohibition of] "it and its offspring," it is [a matter of] doubt.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 24a:13:1.hebrew: ראה חזיר שהוא כרוך אחר רחל - קצת קשה: דנקט חזיר ולא גמל משום דסבר כר' שמעון, דאסר קלוט היוצא מן הטהור, ואפי' היה ידוע שהוא בנה של רחל היה נאסר באכילה? ומיהו, מצינן למימר: דאגב דנקט רחל, שהיא בהמה דקה, נקט חזיר. א"נ, ניחא למינקט למילתיה ככולי עלמא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 24a:13:1.english: “[If] one saw a pig that is trailing after a ewe” - It is somewhat difficult [to suggest] that he specified a pig and not a camel because he holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who forbade an uncloven-hoofed [animal] that emerges from a kosher [animal], such that even if it were known that it is the ewe’s offspring, it would be forbidden for consumption? However, we can say that since he mentioned a ewe, which is a small animal, he mentioned a pig [which is also a small animal]. Alternatively, he preferred to state his ruling in accordance with everyone.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 24a:2:1.hebrew: ופלוגתא דברייתא פלוגתא היא - וא"ת: דר' יוסי בן המשולם נמי פליגי עליה ממה נפשך דברייתא, מדאיצטריך לפסוק הלכה כמותו? וי"ל: דשמא אין מחלוקת שנויה לא במשנה ולא בברייתא, אלא דקים ליה דפליגי רבנן עליה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 24a:2:1.english: "And a dispute in a baraita is a dispute" - And if you say: With regard to Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam as well, [the Rabbis] disagree with him, in any case [in] a baraita, since it was necessary [for Rav] to rule the halakha in accordance with him? And one can say: Perhaps no dispute is taught either in a Mishnah or in a baraita; rather, he was certain that the Rabbis disagreed with him.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 24a:5:1.hebrew: הנכנס לתוך עדרו בלילה כו' ולמחר השכים כו' - תימה: למה ליה למינקט בענין זה? לימא: "הנכנס לתוך עדרו וראה זכרים תלוים כו' ונקבות כו'"! וי"ל, דלרבותא נקט הכי: דאע"ג דודאי היתה תחלת לידתן בלילה, שעדיין אין האמהות מכירין בוולדותיהן, ודרכן לטעות בלילה ובא לו בנה של זו אצל זו — אפי' הכי לא חיישינן:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 24a:5:1.english: "One who enters amid his flock at night, etc., and on the next day he arose, etc." - It is puzzling: Why did he need to formulate [the case] in this manner? Let him say: "One who enters amid his flock and sees males nursing, etc., and females, etc."! And one can say that he formulated [it] this way to teach a novel point: for even though the beginning of their birth was certainly at night, when the mothers do not yet recognize their offspring and it is their way to make an error at night such that the young of this [mother] comes to that [mother] — even so, we are not concerned.
